# ST-Link Auto Debug

Local VS Code extension for STM32CubeMX projects on this ARM (Asahi) machine.
For every project (`.ioc`) in the workspace it offers to create what is needed to build,
flash and debug on a real board with native OpenOCD + GDB, and offers to flash
or debug when an ST-Link is connected. Nothing is tied to one project: the MCU,
board, build system and ELF are read from each project.

## Generated files (`stlinkAutodebug.generateFiles`: ask (default) | auto | off)

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `<project>/openocd.cfg` | `interface/stlink.cfg` + the target for `Mcu.Family` (STM32F4 → `stm32f4x.cfg`) |
| `.vscode/tasks.json` | **Build &lt;name&gt;** and **Flash &lt;name&gt; (ST-Link)** (flash builds first) |
| `.vscode/launch.json` | **Debug &lt;name&gt; (ST-Link)**: builds, flashes, stops at your breakpoints |
| | **Debug &lt;name&gt; (ACII Simulator)** (when the simulator is found): F5 on it builds, opens or restarts the simulator and attaches, like **ACII** with Debug ticked, also after the panel was closed |
| `.vscode/c_cpp_properties.json` | IntelliSense for the C/C++ extension: the Debug include paths and defines from `.cproject` (hover docs, go to definition). Only created if missing |

Debugging (board or simulator) adds a function breakpoint on `main` to the
Breakpoints view if there is none (`stlinkAutodebug.stopAtMain`), so a session
stops at the start; untick or remove it there.

While paused, program time stands still (SysTick stops with the core, on the
board too) and a step runs only microseconds of it, so a debounce or
`HAL_Delay` never completes when stepping. The ⌚ button in the debug toolbar
(*ST-Link: Advance Program Time*) adds `stlinkAutodebug.advanceTimeMs` (100) to
the HAL tick, `uwTick`, as if that much time had passed.

In the ACII simulator a step over code that waits for time (`while (!tickPass())`,
`HAL_Delay`) would otherwise never end, so while a step is still running after
1.5 s the extension does that by itself every 0.5 s, through the Renode monitor,
until the step stops (`stlinkAutodebug.autoAdvanceSteps`, on by default).

Holding **F10** / **F11** / **Shift+F11** keeps stepping until the key is
released, at `stlinkAutodebug.heldStepRate` (8) steps a second
(`stlinkAutodebug.holdToStep`). It works from the key repeat: VS Code reports
no key release, so holding a toolbar button does not repeat.

Offered (never written without asking) when the project opens, when a new `.ioc` appears, and when its build
system appears later (CubeIDE's `Debug/makefile`, CubeMX's `CMakePresets.json`).
Missing entries are added; an entry is only updated while it is still exactly
what the extension wrote, so your edits are kept. Run *ST-Link: Set Up Project
for Board Debugging* to do it by hand.

Build systems:

- STM32CubeIDE projects (`Debug/makefile`): `stm32-make -jN all` in `Debug/`.
- CubeMX CMake projects (`CMakePresets.json`): `cube cmake --preset Debug`
  (first time) then `cube cmake --build --preset Debug`. Not yet tested here:
  the STM32F4 firmware package needed to generate one is not installed.
- Neither: Flash/Debug use the newest existing `.elf`.

A `Debug/makefile` generated by STM32CubeIDE on Windows has the project's
`C:\...` path in it (the linker script), and make fails with "multiple target
patterns". The extension replaces such paths with relative ones when the
project opens, when CubeIDE rewrites the makefile, and before a simulator build.
Objects compiled there are deleted too (their debug info names `C:\...`
sources, so the debugger could not show the code), and the next build compiles
them here.

Debugging runs `gdb` with `target remote | openocd -c "gdb_port pipe"` (as cppdbg's
`miDebuggerServerAddress`, so Pause and breakpoints added while running work):
no TCP port, OpenOCD exits with the session, paths with spaces work. OpenOCD's
log goes to `.vscode/openocd.log`; when a session fails, its first error is
shown with a hint.

## When an ST-Link is connected (`stlinkAutodebug.onConnect`: ask | debug | flash | nothing)

Loads only in workspaces containing a `.ioc`. The probe is checked when the
project opens and on USB hotplug events (`stlinkAutodebug.watchUsb`; inotify on
`/dev` and `/dev/bus/usb`, no polling). On Apple Silicon `/dev/bus/usb` only
exists while something is plugged in, hence the watch on `/dev`.

## ACII simulator (no board needed)

**ACII** in the status bar (or ▶ in the editor title of a C file, or *ST-Link:
Build & Run in ACII Simulator*) builds the project and runs its ELF in the ACII
simulator, the course's Renode model of the NUCLEO-F401RE with the LED&KEY
module. The simulator panel opens if it isn't open yet, and is restarted in
place on later runs.

The **Debug** checkbox next to it in the status bar (`$(circle-large-outline) Debug`
/ `$(pass-filled) Debug`; also *☐/☑ Debug in ACII Simulator* in the ▶ dropdown,
and the `stlinkAutodebug.simulator.debug` setting) picks what happens:

- off: just run it.
- on: the simulator waits at reset ("Esperar al depurador"), GDB attaches to
  `localhost:3333` and it stops at your breakpoints (even in the startup code). Stopping the debug session leaves the
  program running in the simulator.

*Build & Run (no debugger)* and *Build & Debug* ignore the checkbox. The
simulator is found from its menu entry (`acii-simulador.desktop`) or
`~/Downloads/ACII_Simulador`; set `stlinkAutodebug.simulator.path` otherwise.
The extension drives the panel with `simulador-acii.sh --ordenes` (JSON
orders on stdin, `@event` lines on stdout, logged to the *ST-Link Auto Debug*
output).

## Host helpers (in `~/.local/bin`)

- `muvm-run CMD...`: run a command in the muvm VM in the current directory,
  streaming output and returning its exit status (plain `muvm` returns at once).
- `stm32-make`: `make` in the VM with STM32CubeIDE's x86_64 GNU toolchain (FEX).
- `cube`: ST's x86_64 STM32Cube CLI in the VM.

## Build and install

```bash
python3 pack.py && code --install-extension stlink-autodebug-0.4.14.vsix --force
```
